questions.question_text: Let $f$ be a differentiable function on $\mathbb{R}$ such that $f(2) \neq 1$, $f'(2) = 4$. Let $\lim_{x \to 0} (f(2+x))^{3/x} = e^\alpha$. Then the number of times the curve $y = 4x^3 - 4x^2 - 4(\alpha - 7)x - \alpha$ meets the $x$-axis is:
questions.solution_text: Evaluate the limit: $\lim_{x \to 0}(f(2+x))^{3/x}$. This is of the form $1^\infty$ if $f(2) = 1$, but we use the standard form. $\lim_{x\to 0} (f(2+x))^{3/x} = e^{\lim_{x\to 0} \frac{3(f(2+x)-1)}{x}}$. Using L'Hopital or definition of derivative: $\lim_{x\to 0} \frac{f(2+x)-1}{x} = \lim_{x\to 0} \frac{f(2+x)-f(2)}{x} = f'(2) = 4$ (since $f(2)=1$ must hold for the limit to be finite). So $e^\alpha = e^{3 \times 4} = e^{12}$, giving $\alpha = 12$. Now the curve: $y = 4x^3 - 4x^2 - 4(12-7)x - 12 = 4x^3 - 4x^2 - 20x - 12$. Factor: $4(x^3 - x^2 - 5x - 3)$. Test $x = -1$: $-1-1+5-3=0$. So $(x+1)$ is a factor. Dividing: $x^3-x^2-5x-3 = (x+1)(x^2-2x-3) = (x+1)(x+1)(x-3) = (x+1)^2(x-3)$. Roots: $x = -1$ (double), $x = 3$. The curve meets x-axis at 2 distinct points but touches at $x=-1$. Total times it meets (counting multiplicities): $x=-1$ (touches, counts as 1 crossing-type contact) and $x=3$. So it meets x-axis 2 times.

questions.question_text: The sum of the infinite series $\cot^{-1}\left(\frac{7}{4}\right) + \cot^{-1}\left(\frac{19}{4}\right) + \cot^{-1}\left(\frac{39}{4}\right) + \cot^{-1}\left(\frac{67}{4}\right) + \cdots$ is:
questions.solution_text: The $n$-th term denominator sequence: $7/4, 19/4, 39/4, 67/4, \ldots$ Numerators: $7, 19, 39, 67, \ldots$ Differences: $12, 20, 28, \ldots$ (AP with common difference 8). So $a_n = 4n^2 + 3$. Thus $T_n = \cot^{-1}\left(\frac{4n^2+3}{4}\right) = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{4}{4n^2+3}\right)$. Rewrite: $\frac{4}{4n^2+3} = \frac{(2n+\frac{1}{2}) - (2n-\frac{1}{2})}{1+(2n+\frac{1}{2})(2n-\frac{1}{2})} = \tan^{-1}(n+\frac{1}{2}) - \tan^{-1}(n-\frac{1}{2})$ (telescoping). So $T_n = \tan^{-1}(n+\frac{1}{2}) - \tan^{-1}(n-\frac{1}{2})$. Partial sum: $S_N = \tan^{-1}(N+\frac{1}{2}) - \tan^{-1}(\frac{1}{2})$. As $N \to \infty$: $S_\infty = \frac{\pi}{2} - \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$.

questions.question_text: Let the product of $\omega_1 = (8 + i)\sin\theta + (7 + 4i)\cos\theta$ and $\omega_2 = (1 + 8i)\sin\theta + (4 + 7i)\cos\theta$ be $\alpha + i\beta$, $i = \sqrt{-1}$. Let $p$ and $q$ be the maximum and the minimum values of $\alpha + \beta$ respectively. Then $p + q$ is equal to:
questions.solution_text: Let $s = \sin\theta$, $c = \cos\theta$. $\omega_1 = (8s+7c) + i(s+4c)$, $\omega_2 = (s+4c) + i(8s+7c)$. Product $\omega_1\omega_2 = [(8s+7c)(s+4c) - (s+4c)(8s+7c)] + i[(8s+7c)^2 + (s+4c)^2]$. Real part $= 0$, so $\alpha = 0$. $\beta = (8s+7c)^2 + (s+4c)^2 = 64s^2 + 112sc + 49c^2 + s^2 + 8sc + 16c^2 = 65s^2 + 120sc + 65c^2 = 65(s^2+c^2) + 120sc = 65 + 60\sin 2\theta$. So $\alpha + \beta = 65 + 60\sin 2\theta$. Maximum $p = 65 + 60 = 125$, minimum $q = 65 - 60 = 5$. $p + q = 130$.

questions.question_text: Let the values of $p$, for which the shortest distance between the lines $\dfrac{x+1}{3} = \dfrac{y}{4} = \dfrac{z}{5}$ and $\vec{r} = (p\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}) + \lambda(2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 4\hat{k})$ is $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{6}}$, be $a, b$ ($a < b$). Then the length of the latus rectum of the ellipse $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2} + \dfrac{y^2}{b^2} = 1$ is:
questions.solution_text: Line 1 passes through $A=(-1,0,0)$ with direction $\vec{p}=(3,4,5)$. Line 2 passes through $B=(p,2,1)$ with direction $\vec{q}=(2,3,4)$. $\vec{a}-\vec{b} = (-1-p,-2,-1)$. $\vec{p}\times\vec{q} = \begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\3&4&5\\2&3&4\end{vmatrix} = \hat{i}(16-15)-\hat{j}(12-10)+\hat{k}(9-8) = (1,-2,1)$. $|\vec{p}\times\vec{q}| = \sqrt{1+4+1}=\sqrt{6}$. Shortest distance $= \frac{|(-1-p,-2,-1)\cdot(1,-2,1)|}{\sqrt{6}} = \frac{|-1-p+4-1|}{\sqrt{6}} = \frac{|-p+2|}{\sqrt{6}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}$. So $|-p+2|=1$, giving $p=1$ or $p=3$. So $a=1, b=3$. Ellipse: $\frac{x^2}{1}+\frac{y^2}{9}=1$ with $b>a$. Latus rectum $= \frac{2a^2}{b} = \frac{2\times1}{3} = \frac{2}{3}$.

questions.question_text: The axis of a parabola is the line $y = x$ and its vertex and focus are in the first quadrant at distances $\sqrt{2}$ and $2\sqrt{2}$ units from the origin, respectively. If the point $(1, k)$ lies on the parabola, then a possible value of $k$ is:
questions.solution_text: Axis is $y=x$. Vertex at distance $\sqrt{2}$ from origin along $y=x$: vertex $= (1,1)$. Focus at distance $2\sqrt{2}$ from origin along $y=x$: focus $= (2,2)$. Directrix is perpendicular to $y=x$ at vertex, i.e., $x+y=2$ shifted: directrix is $x+y=0$ (the line at distance $\sqrt{2}$ from vertex on opposite side from focus). For point $P(1,k)$ on parabola: distance from $P$ to focus = distance from $P$ to directrix. $\sqrt{(1-2)^2+(k-2)^2} = \frac{|1+k|}{\sqrt{2}}$. $1+(k-2)^2 = \frac{(1+k)^2}{2}$. $2[1+k^2-4k+4] = 1+2k+k^2$. $2+2k^2-8k+8=1+2k+k^2$. $k^2-10k+9=0$. $(k-1)(k-9)=0$. $k=1$ or $k=9$. $k=1$ gives the vertex point, so $k=9$.

questions.question_text: Let the domains of the functions $f(x) = \log_4 \log_3 \log_7 (8 - \log_2(x^2 + 4x + 5))$ and $g(x) = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{7x+10}{x-2}\right)$ be $(\alpha, \beta)$ and $[\gamma, \delta]$, respectively. Then $\alpha^2 + \beta^2 + \gamma^2 + \delta^2$ is equal to:
questions.solution_text: For $f(x)$: Need $\log_7(8-\log_2(x^2+4x+5)) > 0$, so $8 - \log_2(x^2+4x+5) > 1$, i.e., $\log_2(x^2+4x+5) < 7$... Actually work from inside out. Need $\log_3\log_7(\cdot) > 0 \Rightarrow \log_7(\cdot) > 1$. Need $8-\log_2(x^2+4x+5) > 7$, so $\log_2(x^2+4x+5) < 1$, so $x^2+4x+5 < 2$, i.e., $x^2+4x+3 < 0$, $(x+1)(x+3)<0$, so $x \in (-3,-1)$. Domain of $f$: $\alpha=-3, \beta=-1$. For $g(x)$: Need $-1 \le \frac{7x+10}{x-2} \le 1$. Case 1: $\frac{7x+10}{x-2} \ge -1 \Rightarrow \frac{7x+10+x-2}{x-2} \ge 0 \Rightarrow \frac{8x+8}{x-2} \ge 0 \Rightarrow x \le -1$ or $x > 2$. Case 2: $\frac{7x+10}{x-2} \le 1 \Rightarrow \frac{7x+10-x+2}{x-2} \le 0 \Rightarrow \frac{6x+12}{x-2} \le 0 \Rightarrow -2 \le x < 2$. Intersection: $x \in [-2,-1]$. So $\gamma=-2, \delta=-1$. $\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2+\delta^2 = 9+1+4+1 = 15$.

questions.question_text: A line passing through the point $A(-2, 0)$ touches the parabola $P : y^2 = x - 2$ at the point $B$ in the first quadrant. The area of the region bounded by the line $AB$, parabola $P$ and the $x$-axis is:
questions.solution_text: Tangent from $A(-2,0)$ to $y^2 = x-2$. Line through $A$: $y = m(x+2)$. Substituting into parabola: $m^2(x+2)^2 = x-2$. For tangency, discriminant = 0. Let $y = m(x+2)$, so $x = y/m - 2$. Sub into $y^2 = x-2$: $y^2 = y/m - 4$, $m y^2 - y + 4m = 0$. Discriminant = $1 - 16m^2 = 0$, so $m = 1/4$ (first quadrant). Tangent: $y = \frac{1}{4}(x+2)$. Point of tangency $B$: $y = \frac{1}{4}(x+2)$ and $y^2=x-2$. $\frac{(x+2)^2}{16} = x-2$, $(x+2)^2 = 16(x-2)$, $x^2+4x+4=16x-32$, $x^2-12x+36=0$, $(x-6)^2=0$, $x=6$, $y=2$. So $B=(6,2)$. Area between line $AB$, parabola and x-axis: $A = \int_0^2 [(y^2+2) - (4y-2)]\,dy = \int_0^2 (y^2 - 4y + 4)\,dy = \int_0^2 (y-2)^2 dy = \left[\frac{(y-2)^3}{3}\right]_0^2 = 0 - \frac{(-8)}{3} = \frac{8}{3}$.

questions.question_text: Let the matrix $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$ satisfy $A^n = A^{n-2} + A^2 - I$ for $n \geq 3$. Then the sum of all the elements of $A^{50}$ is:
questions.solution_text: Using the recurrence $A^n = A^{n-2} + A^2 - I$: $A^{50} = A^{48} + A^2 - I = A^{46} + 2(A^2-I) = \ldots = A^2 + 24(A^2-I) = 25A^2 - 24I$. Compute $A^2 = A \cdot A$: $A^2 = \begin{bmatrix}1&0&0\\1&0&1\\0&1&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1&0&0\\1&0&1\\0&1&0\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}1&0&0\\1&1&0\\1&0&1\end{bmatrix}$. Then $A^{50} = 25\begin{bmatrix}1&0&0\\1&1&0\\1&0&1\end{bmatrix} - 24\begin{bmatrix}1&0&0\\0&1&0\\0&0&1\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}1&0&0\\25&1&0\\25&0&1\end{bmatrix}$. Sum of elements $= 1+0+0+25+1+0+25+0+1 = 53$.

questions.question_text: Let for two distinct values of $p$ the lines $y = x + p$ touch the ellipse $E: \dfrac{x^2}{4^2} + \dfrac{y^2}{3^2} = 1$ at the points $A$ and $B$. Let the line $y = x$ intersect $E$ at the points $C$ and $D$. Then the area of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is equal to:
questions.solution_text: Ellipse $\frac{x^2}{16}+\frac{y^2}{9}=1$. Tangent $y=x+p$ touches ellipse when $p^2 = 16(1)^2 + 9(1)^2 = 25$, so $p = \pm 5$. Points of tangency for $y=x+p$ with slope $m=1$: $\left(\frac{-a^2m}{\sqrt{a^2m^2+b^2}}, \frac{b^2}{\sqrt{a^2m^2+b^2}}\right) = \left(\frac{-16}{5}, \frac{9}{5}\right)$ and $\left(\frac{16}{5}, \frac{-9}{5}\right)$. So $A=(-16/5, 9/5)$, $B=(16/5, -9/5)$. For $y=x$ intersecting ellipse: $x^2/16 + x^2/9 = 1$, $x^2(9+16)/144=1$, $x^2=144/25$, $x=\pm 12/5$. $C=(12/5, 12/5)$, $D=(-12/5, -12/5)$. Area of quadrilateral $ABCD$ using shoelace or area of triangle $ABD$ times 2. Area = 24.

questions.question_text: If a curve $y = y(x)$ passes through the point $\left(1, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ and satisfies the differential equation $(7x^4 \cot y - e^x \csc y)\dfrac{dx}{dy} = x^5$, $x \geq 1$, then at $x = 2$, the value of $\cos y$ is:
questions.solution_text: Rewrite: $\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{x^5}{7x^4\cot y - e^x\csc y}$. Rearranging: $(7x^4\cot y - e^x\csc y)dx = x^5 dy$... Better: $\frac{dx}{dy} = \frac{x^5}{7x^4\cot y - e^x\csc y}$ is given. Rewrite as linear ODE in $t = \cos y$: Multiply both sides of $7x^4\cot y\frac{dx}{dy} - e^x\csc y\frac{dx}{dy} = x^5$. Dividing by $x^5$: this is complex. Let $t = -\cos y$, $\frac{dt}{dx} = \sin y \frac{dy}{dx}$. From the DE: $\sin y\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{7\cot y - e^x/x^4\cdot\csc y}{1}$... Using the given approach: let $-\cos y = t$. The DE becomes $\frac{dt}{dx} + \frac{7t}{x} = \frac{-e^x}{x^5}$. IF $= x^7$. $t x^7 = -\int x^2 e^x dx = -(x^2e^x - 2xe^x + 2e^x) + C$. At $x=1, y=\pi/2$: $t=0$. $0 = -(e-2e+2e)+C = -e+C$, so $C=e$. At $x=2$: $t\cdot128 = -(4e^2-4e^2+2e^2)+e = -2e^2+e+... $ Wait: $\int x^2 e^x dx = e^x(x^2-2x+2)$. $t\cdot x^7 = -e^x(x^2-2x+2)+C$. At $x=1,t=0$: $0=-e(1-2+2)+C = -e+C$, $C=e$. At $x=2$: $128t = -e^2(4-4+2)+e = -2e^2+e$. $t = \frac{e-2e^2}{128} = \frac{-(2e^2-e)}{128}$. So $\cos y = -t = \frac{2e^2-e}{128}$.

Let $C$ pass through the foci $F_1$ and $F_2$ of $E$ such that the circle $C$ and the ellipse $E$ intersect at four points. Let $P$ be one of these four points. If the area of the triangle $PF_1F_2$ is 30 and the length of the major axis of $E$ is 17, then the distance between the foci of $E$ is:
questions.solution_text: Major axis $2a = 17$, so $a = 17/2$. Circle passes through foci, so radius $r = ae$ (distance from centre to focus). $P$ is on ellipse: $PF_1 + PF_2 = 2a = 17$. $P$ is on circle: $PO = c = ae$ where $F_1F_2 = 2c$. Since $PF_1 = 12$ and $PF_2 = 5$ (or vice versa), check: $12+5=17$ ✓. Area $= \frac{1}{2}PF_1 \cdot PF_2 = \frac{1}{2}\cdot12\cdot5=30$ ✓. $F_1F_2$: using Pythagorean theorem since $P$ is on circle with $F_1, F_2$ as diameter... $PF_1^2 + PF_2^2 = F_1F_2^2$ if angle is 90°. $144+25=169=13^2$. So $F_1F_2 = 13$.

Square of area $= \frac{9\cdot24}{4} = 54$.

questions.question_text: If $\alpha$ is a root of the equation $x^2 + x + 1 = 0$ and $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{n}\left(\alpha^k + \dfrac{1}{\alpha^k}\right)^2 = 20$, then $n$ is equal to ___.
questions.solution_text: $\alpha = \omega$ (cube root of unity). $\left(\alpha^k + \frac{1}{\alpha^k}\right)^2 = \alpha^{2k}+\frac{1}{\alpha^{2k}}+2 = \omega^{2k}+\omega^{-2k}+2 = \omega^{2k}+\omega^{k}+2$ (since $\omega^{-2k}=\omega^{k}$ when $k$ is multiple of 3). $\sum_{k=1}^n(\omega^{2k}+\omega^k+2)=20$. The sums $\sum\omega^k$ and $\sum\omega^{2k}$ cycle with period 3: sum over 3 terms = 0. Testing $n=3m+2$ (since answer is 11 = 3·3+2): $n=11$. Sum of $\omega^k$ for $k=1$ to $11$: $= -1+\omega^2+\omega = -1+(-1) = -2$... Actually $\sum_{k=1}^{11}\omega^k = \omega\frac{1-\omega^{11}}{1-\omega} = \omega\frac{1-\omega^2}{1-\omega} = \omega(1+\omega)= \omega+\omega^2=-1$. Similarly $\sum\omega^{2k}=-1$. So sum $= -1+(-1)+2\cdot11=20$. $\therefore n=11$.

questions.question_text: If $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{\left(\sqrt{1+x^2}+x\right)^{10}}{\left(\sqrt{1+x^2}-x\right)^9}\,dx = \dfrac{1}{m}\left(\left(\sqrt{1+x^2}+x\right)^n\left(n\sqrt{1+x^2}-x\right)\right) + C$ where $C$ is the constant of integration and $m, n \in \mathbb{N}$, then $m + n$ is equal to ___.
questions.solution_text: Rationalize by multiplying numerator and denominator by $(\sqrt{1+x^2}+x)^9$: integrand becomes $(\sqrt{1+x^2}+x)^{19}$ (since $(\sqrt{1+x^2}+x)(\sqrt{1+x^2}-x)=1$). Let $t = \sqrt{1+x^2}+x$, then $\sqrt{1+x^2}-x = 1/t$. $dt = (x/\sqrt{1+x^2}+1)dx = \frac{\sqrt{1+x^2}+x}{\sqrt{1+x^2}}dx = \frac{t}{\sqrt{1+x^2}}dx$. Also $\sqrt{1+x^2} = \frac{1}{2}(t+1/t)$, $dx = \frac{dt}{t}\cdot\frac{1}{2}(t+1/t) = \frac{1}{2}(1+1/t^2)dt$. $I = \int t^{19}\cdot\frac{1}{2}(1+t^{-2})dt = \frac{1}{2}\int(t^{19}+t^{17})dt = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{t^{20}}{20}+\frac{t^{18}}{18}\right)+C = \frac{t^{19}}{360}\left(9t+\frac{10}{t}\right)+C = \frac{t^{19}}{360}(9t+10/t) = \frac{t^{19}}{360}\cdot\frac{9t^2+10}{t}$. Since $t=\sqrt{1+x^2}+x$ and $1/t=\sqrt{1+x^2}-x$: $9t = 9(\sqrt{1+x^2}+x)$, $10/t = 10(\sqrt{1+x^2}-x)$. $9t+10/t = 19\sqrt{1+x^2}-x$. So $I = \frac{t^{19}}{360}(19\sqrt{1+x^2}-x)+C = \frac{1}{360}(\sqrt{1+x^2}+x)^{19}(19\sqrt{1+x^2}-x)+C$. Thus $m=360, n=19$, $m+n=379$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: A card from a pack of 52 cards is lost. From the remaining 51 cards, $n$ cards are drawn and are found to be spades. If the probability of the lost card to be a spade is $\dfrac{11}{50}$, then $n$ is equal to ___.
questions.solution_text: Let the lost card be a spade (probability $13/52=1/4$) or not. If lost is a spade: 12 spades remain in 51 cards, prob of drawing $n$ spades $= \binom{12}{n}/\binom{51}{n}$. If lost is not a spade: 13 spades in 51, prob $= \binom{13}{n}/\binom{51}{n}$. By Bayes': $P(\text{lost}=\text{spade}|n\text{ spades drawn}) = \frac{\frac{1}{4}\cdot\binom{12}{n}/\binom{51}{n}}{\frac{1}{4}\cdot\binom{12}{n}/\binom{51}{n}+\frac{3}{4}\cdot\binom{13}{n}/\binom{51}{n}} = \frac{\binom{12}{n}}{\binom{12}{n}+3\binom{13}{n}}$. Set equal to $11/50$: $50\binom{12}{n}=11\binom{12}{n}+33\binom{13}{n}$. $39\binom{12}{n}=33\binom{13}{n}$. $\frac{\binom{13}{n}}{\binom{12}{n}}=\frac{39}{33}=\frac{13}{11}$. $\frac{13!/(n!(13-n)!)}{12!/(n!(12-n)!)} = \frac{13}{13-n} = \frac{13}{11}$. So $13-n=11$, $n=2$.

questions.question_text: A radioactive material $P$ first decays into $Q$ and then $Q$ decays to non-radioactive material $R$. Which of the following figure represents time dependent mass of $P$, $Q$ and $R$?

options.text: Graph showing P decreasing, Q rising then falling, R continuously rising (option 1 figure)
Graph showing P exponentially decreasing, Q rising to a peak then falling, R continuously rising to plateau (option 2 figure)
Graph showing P and Q together with R (option 3 figure)
Graph showing P rapidly decreasing, R and Q shown differently (option 4 figure)

questions.solution_text: $P \to Q \to R$. $P$ decays exponentially (always decreasing). $Q$ first increases (being produced from $P$) then decreases (decays to $R$) — bell-shaped. $R$ continuously increases from zero as it accumulates. Option (2) correctly shows these behaviors.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: There are '$n$' number of identical electric bulbs, each designed to draw a power $p$ independently from the mains supply. They are now joined in series across the main supply. The total power drawn by the combination is:
questions.solution_text: Each bulb has resistance $R = V^2/p$. In series, $R_s = nR$. Total power $P_s = V^2/R_s = V^2/(nR) = p/n$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Consider a rectangular sheet of solid material of length $\ell = 9$ cm and width $d = 4$ cm. The coefficient of linear expansion is $\alpha = 3.1 \times 10^{-5}$ K$^{-1}$ at room temperature and one atmospheric pressure. The mass of sheet $m = 0.1$ kg and the specific heat capacity $C_v = 900$ J kg$^{-1}$K$^{-1}$. If the amount of heat supplied to the material is $8.1 \times 10^2$ J then change in area of the rectangular sheet is:
questions.solution_text: $\Delta Q = ms\Delta T$: $810 = 0.1\times900\times\Delta T$, so $\Delta T = 9$ K. $A_0 = 9\times4 = 36$ cm$^2 = 36\times10^{-4}$ m$^2$. $\Delta A = A_0 \cdot 2\alpha \cdot \Delta T = 36\times10^{-4}\times2\times3.1\times10^{-5}\times9 = 36\times10^{-4}\times5.58\times10^{-4} = 2.009\times10^{-6} \approx 2.0\times10^{-6}$ m$^2$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

**Statement (I):** The dimensions of Planck's constant and angular momentum are same.

**Statement (II):** In Bohr's model electron revolves around the nucleus only in those orbits for which angular momentum is integral multiple of Planck's constant.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect

questions.solution_text: Statement I: $[h] = [ML^2T^{-1}]$ (from $E=hf$, $[h]=[E/f]=ML^2T^{-2}/T^{-1}=ML^2T^{-1}$). Angular momentum $L = mvr$, $[L]=[ML^2T^{-1}]$. Same dimensions. Statement I is TRUE. Statement II: In Bohr's model, $mvr = n\frac{h}{2\pi}$, i.e., angular momentum is integral multiple of $h/2\pi$ (not $h$). So Statement II is incorrect.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A cylindrical rod of length 1 m and radius 4 cm is mounted vertically. It is subjected to a shear force of $10^5$ N at the top. Considering infinitesimally small displacement in the upper edge, the angular displacement $\theta$ of the rod axis from its original position would be: (shear modulus, $G = 10^{10}$ N/m$^2$)
questions.solution_text: Shear stress $= F/A = 10^5/(\pi\times(0.04)^2) = 10^5/(\pi\times16\times10^{-4}) = 10^5/(16\pi\times10^{-4})$. Shear modulus $G = \sigma/\theta$ (shear stress/shear strain). $\theta = \sigma/G = \frac{10^5/(16\pi\times10^{-4})}{10^{10}} = \frac{10^5}{16\pi\times10^{-4}\times10^{10}} = \frac{10^5}{16\pi\times10^6} = \frac{1}{160\pi}$ radian.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: From the combination of resistors with resistance values $R_1 = R_2 = R_3 = 5\,\Omega$ and $R_4 = 10\,\Omega$, which of the following combination is the best circuit to get an equivalent resistance of $6\,\Omega$?

options.text: $R_1$ and $R_2$ in series (top branch), $R_3$ and $R_4$ in series (bottom branch), both in parallel
$R_1$ parallel with $R_2$, in series with $R_3$ parallel with $R_4$

questions.solution_text: Option 1: Two branches in parallel. Branch 1: $R_1+R_2=10\,\Omega$. Branch 2: $R_3+R_4=15\,\Omega$. Parallel: $R_{eq} = \frac{10\times15}{10+15} = \frac{150}{25} = 6\,\Omega$. ✓

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A metallic ring is uniformly charged as shown in figure. $AC$ and $BD$ are two mutually perpendicular diameters. Electric field due to arc $AB$ to '$O$' is '$E$' in magnitude. What would be the magnitude of electric field at '$O$' due to arc $ABC$?
questions.solution_text: Arc $AB$ (quarter circle) produces field $E$ at $O$ directed diagonally (at 45° to both AC and BD). Arc $BC$ (another quarter circle) produces the same magnitude $E$ by symmetry but in a direction perpendicular to arc $AB$'s field. Arc $ABC$ = arc $AB$ + arc $BC$. These two equal fields are perpendicular to each other, so $|E_{ABC}| = \sqrt{E^2+E^2} = \sqrt{2}E$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: There are two vessels filled with an ideal gas where volume of one is double the volume of other. The large vessel contains the gas at 8 kPa at 1000 K while the smaller vessel contains the gas at 7 kPa at 500 K. If the vessels are connected to each other by a thin tube allowing the gas to flow and the temperature of both vessels is maintained at 600 K, at steady state the pressure in the vessels will be (in kPa):
questions.solution_text: Conservation of moles: $n_1+n_2 = n_f$. $\frac{P_1V_1}{T_1}+\frac{P_2V_2}{T_2} = \frac{P_f V_f}{T_f}$. Let $V_2=V$ (small), $V_1=2V$ (large). $\frac{8\times2V}{1000}+\frac{7\times V}{500} = \frac{P_f\times3V}{600}$. $\frac{16V}{1000}+\frac{7V}{500} = \frac{3VP_f}{600}$. $\frac{16}{1000}+\frac{14}{1000} = \frac{P_f}{200}$. $\frac{30}{1000} = \frac{P_f}{200}$. $P_f = 6$ kPa.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: An object is kept at rest at a distance of $3R$ above the earth's surface where $R$ is earth's radius. The minimum speed with which it must be projected so that it does not return to earth is: (Assume $M$ = mass of earth, $G$ = Universal gravitational constant)
questions.solution_text: Object is at distance $3R$ from surface, i.e., $4R$ from earth's center. For escape from this height: $\frac{1}{2}mv^2 - \frac{GMm}{4R} = 0$ (total energy = 0 for just escaping). $v = \sqrt{\frac{2GM}{4R}} = \sqrt{\frac{GM}{2R}}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Three parallel plate capacitors $C_1$, $C_2$ and $C_3$ each of capacitance $5\,\mu$F are connected as shown in figure. The effective capacitance between points $A$ and $B$, when the space between the parallel plates of $C_1$ capacitor is filled with a dielectric medium having dielectric constant of 4, is:
questions.solution_text: With dielectric $k=4$: $C_1' = 4\times5 = 20\,\mu$F. $C_1'$ in series with $C_2$: $C_{12} = \frac{20\times5}{20+5} = \frac{100}{25} = 4\,\mu$F. $C_{12}$ in parallel with $C_3$: $C_{eq} = 4+5 = 9\,\mu$F.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text:
The displacement $x$ versus time graph is shown below. [Graph with various segments from $t=0$ to $t=9$s.] Choose the correct statements:
(A) The average velocity during 0 to 3 s is 10 m/s
(B) The average velocity during 3 to 5 s is 0 m/s
(C) The instantaneous velocity at $t = 2$ s is 5 m/s
(D) The average velocity during 5 to 7 s and instantaneous velocity at $t = 6.5$ s are equal
(E) The average velocity from $t = 0$ to $t = 9$ s is zero
questions.solution_text: (A) Average velocity 0 to 3s: $(5-0)/3 = 5/3$ m/s, NOT 10. FALSE. (B) Average velocity 3 to 5s: $(5-5)/2=0$. TRUE. (C) At $t=2$s, slope (instantaneous velocity) = 5 m/s (from graph, $x$ goes from 0 to 5 in 0 to 2s... slope = 5/2... but per the graph from B to C is slope $=5$ m/s from the segment). TRUE. (D) Avg vel 5 to 7s: $(0-5)/2 = -2.5$ m/s. Instantaneous at $t=6.5$s: slope at that point = 10 m/s (from graph). NOT equal. FALSE. (E) Average vel 0 to 9s: displacement $= 0-0=0$, avg $=0$. TRUE. Correct: B, C, E → Option 4.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A wheel is rolling on a plane surface. The speed of a particle on the highest point of the rim is 8 m/s. The speed of the particle on the rim of the wheel at the same level as the centre of wheel, will be:
questions.solution_text: In rolling, $v_{top} = 2v_{cm}$. So $8 = 2v_{cm}$, $v_{cm}=4$ m/s. At the side (level with centre), the point has velocity composed of: translational $v_{cm}=4$ m/s (horizontal) and rotational $v_{cm}=4$ m/s (vertical, since $\omega r = v_{cm}$). Magnitude $= \sqrt{4^2+4^2} = 4\sqrt{2}$ m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A block of mass 25 kg is pulled along a horizontal surface by a force at an angle 45° with the horizontal. The friction coefficient between the block and the surface is 0.25. The displacement of 5 m of the block is: (block travels with uniform velocity)
questions.solution_text: At uniform velocity, $F\cos45° = \mu N = \mu(mg - F\sin45°)$. $F/\sqrt{2} = 0.25(25\times9.8 - F/\sqrt{2})$. $F/\sqrt{2}(1+0.25) = 0.25\times245$. $1.25F/\sqrt{2} = 61.25$. $F = 61.25\sqrt{2}/1.25 = 49\sqrt{2}$ N. Work done by external force = $Fs\cos45° = 49\sqrt{2}\times5\times(1/\sqrt{2}) = 49\times5 = 245$ J.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two polarisers $P_1$ and $P_2$ are placed in such a way that the intensity of the transmitted light will be zero. A third polariser $P_3$ is inserted in between $P_1$ and $P_2$, at the particular angle between $P_2$ and $P_3$. The transmitted intensity of the light passing through all three polarisers is maximum. The angle between the polarisers $P_2$ and $P_3$ is:
questions.solution_text: $P_1$ and $P_2$ are crossed (90° apart). Let $P_3$ make angle $\theta$ with $P_2$. Then $P_3$ makes angle $(90°-\theta)$ with $P_1$. After $P_1$: intensity $I_0$. After $P_3$: $I_0\cos^2(90°-\theta) = I_0\sin^2\theta$. After $P_2$ (angle $\theta$ from $P_3$): $I_0\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta = \frac{I_0}{4}\sin^2 2\theta$. Maximize: $\sin^2 2\theta = 1$, $2\theta = 90°$, $\theta = 45° = \pi/4$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text:
Consider an n-type semiconductor in which $n_e$ and $n_h$ are number of electrons and holes, respectively. Which of the following statements are correct?
(A) Holes are minority carriers
(B) The dopant is a pentavalent atom
(C) $n_e n_h \neq n_i^2$ (where $n_i$ is intrinsic carrier concentration)
(D) $n_e n_h \geq n_i^2$
(E) The holes are not generated due to the donors
questions.solution_text: (A) In n-type, electrons are majority, holes are minority. TRUE. (B) n-type dopant is pentavalent (donates extra electron). TRUE. (C) In doped semiconductor, mass action law: $n_e n_h = n_i^2$ still holds. So $n_e n_h = n_i^2$, meaning (C) is FALSE. (D) $n_e n_h = n_i^2$ (not $\geq$). FALSE. (E) Donors add electrons, not holes. Holes in n-type come from thermal excitation only, not from donors. TRUE. Correct: A, B, E → Option 3.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II:

| List-I | List-II |
|---|---|
| (A) Isobaric | (I) $\Delta Q = \Delta W$ |
| (B) Isochoric | (II) $\Delta Q = \Delta U$ |
| (C) Adiabatic | (III) $\Delta Q = $ zero |
| (D) Isothermal | (IV) $\Delta Q = \Delta U + P\Delta V$ |

$\Delta Q$ = Heat supplied; $\Delta W$ = Work done; $\Delta U$ = Change in internal energy; $P$ = Pressure; $\Delta V$ = Change in volume
questions.solution_text: (A) Isobaric ($P=$ const): $\Delta Q = \Delta U + P\Delta V$ → (IV). (B) Isochoric ($V=$ const, $\Delta V=0$): $\Delta Q = \Delta U$ → (II). (C) Adiabatic ($\Delta Q=0$) → (III). (D) Isothermal ($\Delta U=0$ for ideal gas): $\Delta Q = \Delta W$ → (I). Answer: A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I → Option 3.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Displacement of a wave is expressed as $x(t) = 5\cos\left(628t + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ m. The wavelength of the wave when its velocity is 300 m/s is:
questions.solution_text: $\omega = 628$ rad/s. $v = \omega/k = 300$ m/s, so $k = 628/300$. $\lambda = 2\pi/k = 2\pi\times300/628 = 600\pi/628 \approx 3$ m (since $628 \approx 2\pi\times100$, $\lambda = 300/100 = 3$ m).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A finite size object is placed normal to the principal axis at a distance of 30 cm from a convex mirror of focal length 30 cm. A plane mirror is now placed in such a way that the image produced by both the mirrors coincide with each other. The distance between the two mirrors is:
questions.solution_text: For convex mirror: $1/v - 1/u = 1/f$ (using sign convention: $u=-30$, $f=+30$). $1/v = 1/30 + 1/(-30)$... use $1/v + 1/u = 1/f$ with $u=-30, f=+30$: $1/v = 1/30 - 1/30$... Let me use standard: $1/v + 1/(-30) = 1/30$? No. Mirror formula: $1/f = 1/v + 1/u$ (all with sign). For convex mirror, $f=+30$, object at $u=-30$: $1/v = 1/f - 1/u = 1/30+1/30 = 2/30$... Hmm. Using $1/v+1/u=1/f$, $f=+30$, $u=-30$: $1/v = 1/30+1/30 = 2/30$, $v=15$ cm (virtual image, 15 cm behind mirror). For plane mirror to form same image: plane mirror should be placed so its image coincides. Image of convex mirror is 15 cm behind it = 30+15=45 cm from object on the right side. Plane mirror forms image at same distance behind it. Place plane mirror at 22.5 cm from object, image at 22.5 cm behind it = 45 cm from object. Distance between mirrors = 30 - 22.5 = 7.5 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: In an electromagnetic system, a quantity defined as the ratio of electric dipole moment and magnetic dipole moment has dimension of $[M^P L^0 T^R A^S]$. The value of P and Q are:
questions.solution_text: Electric dipole moment $\vec{p} = q\cdot 2\ell$: $[p] = [C\cdot m] = [A\cdot T\cdot L]$. Magnetic dipole moment $\vec{M} = I\cdot A$: $[M] = [A\cdot L^2]$. Ratio $[p/M] = \frac{ATL}{AL^2} = \frac{T}{L} = L^{-1}T^1A^0M^0$. So $P=0$, $R=1$... but the question says $[M^P L^0 T^R A^S]$. $P=0, R=1, S=0$. But option 4 says $0,-1$. If the ratio is $[M/p]$ instead: $AL^2/ATL = L/T = L^1T^{-1}$. Per the PDF solution: $[P/M] = L^{-1}T = M^0 L^{-1} T^1 A^0$. The dimension is $[M^0 L^{-1} T^1 A^0]$... answer is $(P,Q)=(0,-1)$ likely meaning different notation. Per PDF: answer is option 4 with $P=0, Q=-1$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A particle of charge $1.6\,\mu$C and mass $16\,\mu$g is present in a strong magnetic field of 6.28 T. The particle is then fired perpendicular to magnetic field. The time required for the particle to return to original location for the first time is _______ s. ($\pi = 3.14$)
questions.solution_text: Time period $T = \frac{2\pi m}{qB} = \frac{2\times3.14\times16\times10^{-9}}{1.6\times10^{-6}\times6.28} = \frac{2\times3.14\times16\times10^{-9}}{1.6\times6.28\times10^{-6}} = \frac{100.48\times10^{-9}}{10.048\times10^{-6}} = 0.01$ s. Rounded to nearest integer: $T \approx 0$ s. (NTA answer: 10, but $T=0.01$ s rounds to 0).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A solid sphere with uniform density and radius $R$ is rotating initially with constant angular velocity ($\omega_1$) about its diameter. After some time during the rotation it starts loosing mass at a uniform rate, with no change in its shape. The angular velocity of the sphere when its radius becomes $R/2$ is $x\omega_1$. The value of $x$ is ______.
questions.solution_text: When radius reduces to $R/2$ with no change in shape (density unchanged? or shape preserved). If density is uniform and shape preserved (sphere), mass scales as $r^3$: $m' = M(R/2)^3/R^3 = M/8$. Conservation of angular momentum: $I_1\omega_1 = I_2\omega_2$. $I_1 = \frac{2}{5}MR^2$, $I_2 = \frac{2}{5}\frac{M}{8}\frac{R^2}{4} = \frac{2}{5}\frac{MR^2}{32}$. $\omega_2 = \omega_1\frac{I_1}{I_2} = \omega_1\times32 = 32\omega_1$. So $x=32$.

questions.topic: Double Slit and Single Slit Diffraction
questions.question_text: In a Young's double slit experiment, two slits are located 1.5 mm apart. The distance of screen from slits is 2 m and the wavelength of the source is 400 nm. If the 20 maxima of the double slit pattern are contained within the centre maximum of the single slit diffraction pattern, then the width of each slit is $x \times 10^{-3}$ cm, where $x$-value is ______.
questions.solution_text: Width of central maximum of single slit = $2\lambda D/a$. Width of 20 maxima of double slit = $20\times(\lambda D/d)$. Setting equal: $20\lambda D/d = 2\lambda D/a$. $a = d/10 = 1.5\text{ mm}/10 = 0.15$ mm $= 15\times10^{-3}$ cm. So $x=15$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: An inductor of self inductance 1 H connected in series with a resistor of $100\pi$ ohm and an AC supply of $100\pi$ volt, 50 Hz. Maximum current flowing in the circuit is _______ A.
questions.solution_text: $X_L = \omega L = 2\pi\times50\times1 = 100\pi\,\Omega$. $Z = \sqrt{R^2+X_L^2} = \sqrt{(100\pi)^2+(100\pi)^2} = 100\pi\sqrt{2}\,\Omega$. $V_{rms} = 100\pi$ V (given). $I_{rms} = V_{rms}/Z = 100\pi/(100\pi\sqrt{2}) = 1/\sqrt{2}$ A. $I_{max} = I_{rms}\times\sqrt{2} = 1$ A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The correct order of basicity for the following molecules is: (P) 2-piperidone (N-acyl, cyclic), (Q) N-methyl piperidine with cross conjugation, (R) Quinuclidine (bridged bicyclic amine)
questions.solution_text: (R) Quinuclidine: bridged bicyclic amine with localized lone pair (Bredt's rule isolates LP), most basic. (Q) N-methylpiperidine: LP partially delocalized due to cross conjugation, less basic than R. (P) 2-piperidone: N is part of amide, LP delocalized into C=O, least basic. Order: R > Q > P.

So IE of $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ > IE of $\text{Fe}^{2+}$, meaning $\text{Mn}^{2+} > \text{Fe}^{2+}$. Option (4) says $\text{Mn}^{2+} < \text{Fe}^{2+}$, which is INCORRECT.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which among the following compounds give yellow solid when reacted with NaOI/NaOH?
(A) $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{C}_2\text{H}_5$
(B) $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$
(C) $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$ (acetone)
(D) $\text{CH}_3\text{C(O)OH}$ (acetic acid)
(E) $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$ (propanal)
questions.solution_text: Iodoform test (NaOI/NaOH) gives yellow precipitate (CHI₃) with: methyl ketones ($\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$), acetaldehyde ($\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$), ethanol ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$), and secondary alcohols of type $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)-}$. (A) $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{C}_2\text{H}_5$: has $\text{CH}_3\text{-CH(OH)-}$ group → positive. (B) 1-propanol: no $\text{CH}_3$ adjacent to OH → negative. (C) Acetone: $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ → positive. (D) Acetic acid: oxidation state issue, doesn't give iodoform. (E) Propanal $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$: no $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ or $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)-}$ → negative. Positive: A and C → Option 2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: A dipeptide "$x$" on complete hydrolysis gives "$y$" and "$z$". "$y$" on treatment with aq. HNO₂ produces lactic acid. On the other hand "$z$" on heating gives a cyclic molecule (2,5-diketopiperazine structure shown). Based on the information given, the dipeptide X is:
questions.solution_text: $y$ + HNO₂ → lactic acid. Alanine (CH₃-CH(NH₂)-COOH) + HNO₂ → HO-CH(CH₃)-COOH (lactic acid). So $y$ = alanine. $z$ on heating gives 2,5-diketopiperazine from glycine (H₂N-CH₂-COOH). So $z$ = glycine. Dipeptide $x$ = alanine-glycine.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
In which pairs, the first ion is more stable than the second?
(A) Cyclohexyl-CH₂⁺ with OMe vs cyclohexyl-CH₂⁺ with Me (back bonding)
(B) Diphenyl carbanion with NO₂ groups vs diphenyl carbocation
(C) Benzyl cation vs cyclohexenyl-CH₂⁺
(D) t-Bu⁺ vs t-Bu-OMe⁺
questions.solution_text: (A) Cyclohexyl-CH₂⁺-OMe: back bonding from OMe oxygen stabilizes > simple alkyl carbocation. First > second. TRUE. (B) Carbanion with electron-withdrawing NO₂ groups is more stable than carbocation. First (carbanion-NO₂) is more stable. TRUE. (C) Benzyl cation (resonance stabilized) < cyclohexenyl-CH₂⁺ (also resonance but check). Actually allylic benzyl: benzyl is resonance-stabilized. Cyclohexenyl-CH₂⁺ is allylic and could be similarly or less stable. FALSE. (D) t-Bu⁺ < t-Bu-OMe⁺ since OMe provides back bonding making it more stable. So first < second. FALSE. Correct pairs: A and B → Option 2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

**Statement (I):** Alcohols are formed when alkyl chlorides are treated with aqueous potassium hydroxide by elimination reaction.

**Statement (II):** In alcoholic potassium hydroxide, alkyl chlorides form alkenes by abstracting the hydrogen from the $\beta$-carbon.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct

questions.solution_text: Statement I: Alkyl chlorides with aqueous KOH undergo SN2 (substitution), not elimination, forming alcohols. So 'elimination' is wrong — Statement I is INCORRECT. Statement II: Alcoholic KOH with alkyl chlorides gives elimination (E2), abstracting H from β-carbon to form alkenes. Statement II is CORRECT.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

**Statement (I):** Molal depression constant $K_f$ is given by $\dfrac{M_1 R T_f}{\Delta S_{\text{fus}}}$, where symbols have their usual meaning.

**Statement (II):** $K_f$ for benzene is less than the $K_f$ for water.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer:

options.text: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

questions.solution_text: Statement I: $K_f = \frac{M_1RT_f^2}{\Delta H_{fus}} = \frac{M_1RT_f^2}{T_f\Delta S_{fus}} = \frac{M_1RT_f}{\Delta S_{fus}}$. This is CORRECT. Statement II: $K_f$(benzene) = 5.12 °C/m, $K_f$(water) = 1.86 °C/m. Benzene's $K_f$ > water's $K_f$. So Statement II is INCORRECT. Answer: Option 4.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The IUPAC name of the following compound is: $\text{HC}\equiv\text{C} - \text{CH}_2 - \overset{|}{\underset{|}{\text{CH(OH)}}} - \text{CH}_2 - \text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$
questions.solution_text: Number the chain to give lower locants to multiple bonds: $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\overset{4}{\text{CH(OH)}}-\text{CH}_2-\text{C}\equiv\text{CH}$. Numbering from the double bond end: 1(CH₂=), 2(CH-), 3(CH₂-), 4(CHOH-), 5(CH₂-), 6(C≡), 7(CH). Double bond at 1, triple bond at 6, OH at 4. IUPAC: Hept-1-en-6-yn-4-ol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (Separation of) with List-II (Separation Technique):

| List-I | List-II |
|---|---|
| (A) Aniline from aniline-water mixture | (I) Simple distillation |
| (B) Glycerol from spent-lye in soap industry | (II) Fractional distillation |
| (C) Different fractions of crude oil in petroleum industry | (III) Distillation at reduced pressure |
| (D) Chloroform-Aniline mixture | (IV) Steam distillation |
questions.solution_text: (A) Aniline from water: steam distillation (IV). (B) Glycerol from spent-lye (high BP, decomposes): distillation at reduced pressure (III). (C) Crude oil fractions: fractional distillation (II). (D) CHCl₃-aniline: simple distillation (I). Answer: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I → Option 1.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: A toxic compound "A" when reacted with NaCN in aqueous acidic medium yields an edible cooking component and food preservative 'B'. 'B' is converted to 'C' by diborane and can be used as an additive to petrol to reduce emission. 'C' upon reaction with oleum at 140°C yields an inhalable anesthetic 'D'. Identify 'A', 'B', 'C' and 'D' respectively.

options.text: Methanol; acetic acid; ethanol; diethyl ether
Acetaldehyde; 2-hydroxypropanoic acid; propanoic acid; dipropyl ether

questions.solution_text: A (toxic) + NaCN → B (edible). Methanol (A, toxic) + NaCN in acidic → CH₃OH + NaCN → ... Actually: A = Methanol. Methanol + NaCN doesn't work simply. Per PDF: A=Methanol → B=Acetic acid (via NaCN then hydrolysis). B=acetic acid (food preservative/cooking). B + B₂H₆ (diborane reduces COOH to CH₂OH) → C=Ethanol (petrol additive). C (ethanol) + oleum at 140°C → diethyl ether (D, anesthetic). Answer: Methanol; acetic acid; ethanol; diethyl ether.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Number of Unpaired Electrons in Complexes
questions.question_text: The correct order of $[\text{FeF}_6]^{3-}$, $[\text{CoF}_6]^{3-}$, $[\text{Ni(CN)}_4]^{2-}$ and $[\text{Ni(CO)}_4]$ complex species based on the number of unpaired electrons present is:
questions.solution_text: $[\text{FeF}_6]^{3-}$: Fe³⁺, $d^5$, weak field F⁻ → high spin, 5 unpaired. $[\text{CoF}_6]^{3-}$: Co³⁺, $d^6$, weak field F⁻ → high spin, 4 unpaired. $[\text{Ni(CN)}_4]^{2-}$: Ni²⁺, $d^8$, strong field CN⁻, square planar → 0 unpaired. $[\text{Ni(CO)}_4]$: Ni⁰, $d^{10}$ (4s electrons excite to 3d) → 0 unpaired. Order: 5 > 4 > 0 = 0. Option 4.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Consider the given data:
(a) HCl(g) + 10H₂O(l) → HCl·10H₂O, $\Delta H = -69.01$ kJ mol$^{-1}$
(b) HCl(g) + 40H₂O(l) → HCl·40H₂O, $\Delta H = -72.79$ kJ mol$^{-1}$

Choose the correct statement:

options.text: Dissolution of gas in water is an endothermic process
The heat of solution depends on the amount of solvent.
The heat of dilution for the HCl (HCl·10H₂O to HCl·40H₂O) is 3.78 kJ mol$^{-1}$.
The heat of formation of HCl solution is represented by both (a) and (b)

questions.solution_text: (1) $\Delta H$ is negative, so dissolution is exothermic, not endothermic. FALSE. (2) The two $\Delta H$ values differ (−69.01 vs −72.79 kJ/mol), so heat of solution depends on amount of solvent. TRUE. (3) Heat of dilution = $\Delta H_b - \Delta H_a = -72.79 - (-69.01) = -3.78$ kJ/mol (negative, exothermic). Statement says $+3.78$, which is incorrect magnitude/sign. FALSE. (4) Formation of HCl(g) not accounted for. FALSE. Answer: Option 2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Consider the ground state of chromium atom ($Z = 24$). How many electrons are with Azimuthal quantum number $\ell = 1$ and $\ell = 2$ respectively?
questions.solution_text: Cr ($Z=24$): ground state $1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 3d^5 4s^1$. $\ell=1$ (p-orbitals): $2p^6 + 3p^6 = 12$ electrons. $\ell=2$ (d-orbitals): $3d^5 = 5$ electrons. Answer: 12 and 5.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

**Statement (I):** The first ionisation enthalpy of group 14 elements is higher than the corresponding elements of group 13.

**Statement (II):** Melting points and boiling points of group 13 elements are in general much higher than those the corresponding elements of group 14.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer:

options.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct

questions.solution_text: Statement I: In general, IE₁ increases left to right across period, so Group 14 > Group 13. CORRECT. Statement II: Group 14 elements (C as diamond, Si, Ge) generally have higher melting/boiling points than group 13. Statement II is INCORRECT. Answer: Option 1.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Consider the following plots of log of rate constant $k$ (log $k$) vs $\dfrac{1}{T}$ for three different reactions. The correct order of activation energies of these reactions is (graph shows lines 1, 2, 3 with different slopes):
questions.solution_text: From Arrhenius: $\log k = \log A - \frac{E_a}{2.303RT}$. Slope $= -E_a/2.303R$. Greater magnitude of slope → higher $E_a$. From the graph, slope magnitudes: (2) > (1) > (3). So $E_{a_2} > E_{a_1} > E_{a_3}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: '$X$' is the number of electrons in $t_{2g}$ orbitals of the most stable complex ion among $[\text{Fe(NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$, $[\text{FeCl}_6]^{3-}$, $[\text{Fe(C}_2\text{O}_4)_3]^{3-}$ and $[\text{Fe(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+}$. The nature of oxide of vanadium of the type $V_2O_X$ is:
questions.solution_text: Most stable complex of Fe³⁺ is $[\text{Fe(C}_2\text{O}_4)_3]^{3-}$ (chelation effect, strong field). Fe³⁺ is $d^5$, strong field (oxalate is strong): low spin, $t_{2g}^5 e_g^0$, $X=5$. $V_2O_X$: $V_2O_5$ (where $X=5$, V oxidation state $= +5$). $V_2O_5$ is amphoteric (acts as both acid and base).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The elements of Group 13 with highest and lowest first ionisation enthalpies are respectively:
questions.solution_text: IE₁ order for Group 13: B > Tl > Ga > Al > In. Highest: B. Lowest: In. Answer: B & In → Option 4.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Addition of HBr to Bicyclic Compound
questions.question_text: Consider the following molecule (X) [a bicyclic compound with fused rings containing a double bond]. The structure of X is: (four options showing different bromination products with Br at different positions)
questions.solution_text: The bicyclic compound X undergoes electrophilic addition of HBr. H⁺ adds to form the more stable 3° carbocation (Markovnikov). The 3° carbocation is then attacked by Br⁻ to give the major product. Option (2) shows the correct regiochemistry with Br at the more substituted carbon.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements about ClF₃ ($\text{sp}^3\text{d}$ hybridized):

**Statement (I):** For $\overset{..}{\text{C}}\overset{..}{\ell}\text{F}_3$, all three possible structures may be drawn with LP in different positions.

**Statement (II):** Structure III is most stable, as the orbitals having the lone pairs are axial, where the $\ell p - bp$ repulsion is minimum.

options.text: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect

questions.solution_text: Statement I: For ClF₃ (sp³d), three structural arrangements are possible placing lone pairs in equatorial/axial positions. CORRECT. Statement II: In sp³d hybridization, lone pairs prefer equatorial positions (not axial) to minimize lp-bp repulsions. The actual structure of ClF₃ has lone pairs in equatorial positions (T-shape). So saying lone pairs are axial for maximum stability is INCORRECT. Answer: Option 2.

questions.question_text: Sea water, which can be considered as a 6 molar (6 M) solution of NaCl, has a density of 2 g mL$^{-1}$. The concentration of dissolved oxygen (O₂) in sea water is 5.8 ppm. Then the concentration of dissolved oxygen (O₂) in sea water, is $x \times 10^{-4}$ m. $x$ = ______. (Nearest integer) [Molar mass of NaCl = 58.5 g mol$^{-1}$, Molar mass of O₂ = 32 g mol$^{-1}$]

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The amount of calcium oxide produced on heating 150 kg limestone (75% pure) is ______ kg. (Nearest integer) [Molar mass (in g mol$^{-1}$): Ca-40, O-16, C-12]
questions.solution_text: $\text{CaCO}_3 \to \text{CaO} + \text{CO}_2$. Mass of pure CaCO₃ = 150×75/100 = 112.5 kg. Moles CaCO₃ = 112500/100 = 1125 mol. Moles CaO = 1125 mol. Mass CaO = 1125×56/1000 = 63 kg.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: A metal complex with a formula $\text{MC}\ell_4 \cdot 3\text{NH}_3$ is involved in $\text{sp}^3\text{d}^2$ hybridisation. It upon reaction with excess of AgNO₃ solution gives '$x$' moles of AgCl. Consider '$x$' is equal to the number of lone pairs of electron present in central atom of BrF₅. Then the number of geometrical isomers exhibited by the complex is ______.
questions.solution_text: BrF₅: Br has 5 bonds + 1 lone pair, so 1 lone pair. $x=1$. Complex $\text{MC}\ell_4\cdot3\text{NH}_3$ gives 1 mol AgCl with excess AgNO₃, so 1 ionizable Cl⁻. Formula: $[\text{M(NH}_3)_3\text{Cl}_3]\text{Cl}$. The inner sphere complex $[\text{M(NH}_3)_3\text{Cl}_3]$ with sp³d² (octahedral) has formula $\text{Ma}_3\text{b}_3$: facial (fac) and meridional (mer) isomers. Number of geometrical isomers = 2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Molar Conductance and Degree of Dissociation
questions.question_text: The molar conductance of an infinitely dilute solution of ammonium chloride was found to be 185 S cm² mol$^{-1}$ and the ionic conductance of hydroxyl and chloride ions are 170 and 70 S cm² mol$^{-1}$, respectively. If molar conductance of 0.02 M solution of ammonium hydroxide is 85.5 S cm² mol$^{-1}$, its degree of dissociation is given by $x \times 10^{-1}$. The value of $x$ is ______. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution_text: $\lambda_m^\infty(\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}) = 185$. $\lambda^\infty(\text{NH}_4^+) + \lambda^\infty(\text{Cl}^-) = 185$. $\lambda^\infty(\text{NH}_4^+) = 185-70 = 115$ S cm² mol⁻¹. $\lambda_m^\infty(\text{NH}_4\text{OH}) = \lambda^\infty(\text{NH}_4^+)+\lambda^\infty(\text{OH}^-) = 115+170 = 285$ S cm² mol⁻¹. $\alpha = \lambda_m/\lambda_m^\infty = 85.5/285 = 0.3 = 3\times10^{-1}$. $x=3$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: $x$ mg of Mg(OH)₂ (molar mass = 58) is required to be dissolved in 1.0 L of water to produce a pH of 10.0 at 298 K. The value of $x$ is ______ mg. (Nearest integer) [Given: Mg(OH)₂ is assumed to dissociate completely in H₂O]
questions.solution_text: pH = 10, so pOH = 4, $[\text{OH}^-] = 10^{-4}$ mol/L. Moles of OH⁻ = $10^{-4}$. Since Mg(OH)₂ → Mg²⁺ + 2OH⁻, moles of Mg(OH)₂ = $10^{-4}/2 = 5\times10^{-5}$ mol. Mass = $5\times10^{-5}\times58 = 2.9\times10^{-3}$ g = $2.9$ mg $\approx 3$ mg.
